name: UeWF World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The federation's own top belt, defended every week against the highest-ranked contender who had not already had a shot that month. The Ultimate Lanny held it when the federation went dark in the spring of 1992, and was still recognised as champion when it reopened that May; no match for the start or the end of that reign survives. Carried back from the WeWF wing, whose own newsdesk This Week in Wrestling printed this federation's weekly title results and full rankings through the winter of 1992. The belt's own winter is now dated end to end. Lord Plunder is champion in the newsdesk's own standings of 30 January 1992, at 11-2 — and the same issue's rumour mill says why: “The recent ‘administrative errors’ in the UeWF which allowed Lord Plunder to obtain the World Championship were a direct result of the bribing of the UeWFs chief officer - Harvey Wallbanger.” Mr. B is champion by 15 February at 11-2-1; he hands Admiral Ax the first loss of his career to retain it on 19 February; and on 25 February the Ultimate Lanny beats him with a superplex, called move for move — “ONE! TWO!!.........THREEEEE!!!!!! We've got a new World Champion!!!!!” Three reigns are registered here on that record.
notes: Declared in the federation's own founding document, 19 November 1991 (promotions/uewf/archive/new-pbem-the-uewf-1991-11-19.html), which sets out how it was to be defended. Holder transcribed from the federation's own relaunch call, 14 May 1992. The federation's own inaugural World Championship tournament ran two rounds on 27 December 1991 and both semi-finals on the 28th, and its final — Mr. B against Lucifer — was advertised for a fifth night that no held document carries. The Ultimate Lanny went out of it in the FIRST ROUND, beaten by Lucifer. Whoever won that final, this reign did not begin at the Summit, and the record still does not say when it did. The weekly record survives second-hand, in another federation's own newsdesk, not yet served here. Nine editions of the WeWF's own This Week in Wrestling and its TTTTTT tag tournament, 30 January to 31 March 1992, plus the EMWA's own Kings Of The Ring of 25 March, are held in this project's own Google Groups dumps and are unserved. Between them they carry this federation's own weekly title results week by week, its full ranking tables with win-loss records and points, and two of its own matches staged play-by-play. What they say about THIS belt: the standings table of 15 February 1992 has Mr. B as World Champion at 11-2-1; the roundup of 19 February has Mr. B beating Admiral Ax to retain it, handing Ax the first loss of his career; and the broadcast of 25 February stages the title change itself, play-by-play — The Ultimate Lanny beating Mr. B with a superplex, "We've got a new World Champion!!!!!" — and prints the new table, "World Champion: The Ultimate Lanny (15-3-1) 89". The reign the May 1992 relaunch call recognises therefore begins in the last week of February 1992, and at least two earlier reigns exist that this ledger does not carry: Mr. B's, and whatever Lord Plunder held when the newsdesk's own rumour mill of 30 January 1992 reported "the recent 'administrative errors' in the UeWF which allowed Lord Plunder to obtain the World Championship."

name: UeWF Intercontinental Championship
epitaph: The federation's own second singles belt, defended weekly against the second-ranked contender. Admiral Ax held it into the 1992 hiatus and was still recognised as champion at the relaunch. Carried back from the WeWF wing, whose own newsdesk This Week in Wrestling printed this federation's weekly title results and full rankings through the winter of 1992. Mr. B holds this belt at 10-1-1 in the newsdesk's own standings of 30 January 1992; by 15 February he has the World Championship and Admiral Ax has this one at 10-0-0. Ax then defends it twice on the record — over Lord Plunder on 19 February and over Rage on 25 February — and is 14-1 in the last standings the newsdesk printed.
notes: Declared in the federation's own founding document, 19 November 1991 (promotions/uewf/archive/new-pbem-the-uewf-1991-11-19.html), which sets out how it was to be defended. Holder transcribed from the federation's own relaunch call, 14 May 1992. Where this belt's own first reign began is still not on the record. The weekly record survives second-hand, in another federation's own newsdesk, not yet served here. Nine editions of the WeWF's own This Week in Wrestling and its TTTTTT tag tournament, 30 January to 31 March 1992, plus the EMWA's own Kings Of The Ring of 25 March, are held in this project's own Google Groups dumps and are unserved. Between them they carry this federation's own weekly title results week by week, its full ranking tables with win-loss records and points, and two of its own matches staged play-by-play. What they say about THIS belt: Admiral Ax holds it throughout — 10-0-0 in the table of 15 February 1992, beating Lord Plunder to retain on the 19th, beating Rage to retain on the 25th, and 14-1-0 in the table that week. His single loss in that span is the World Championship match he lost to Mr. B, not a defence of this belt. Nothing in the held record says when the reign began.

name: UeWF Atlantic Championship
epitaph: One of a matched pair of regional belts, defended against any challenger of the champion's own choosing who stood inside the top tenth of the rankings. Pain held it into the 1992 hiatus. Carried back from the WeWF wing, whose own newsdesk This Week in Wrestling printed this federation's weekly title results and full rankings through the winter of 1992. The belt is VACANT in the newsdesk's own standings of 15 February 1992 — Admiral Ax had left it to take the Intercontinental Championship. Biff “the Terror” Jones fills the vacancy on 19 February (“Biff ‘the Terror’ Jones eeked a pin out over Mosh to become the new Atlantic Champion”) and Pain takes it off him on 25 February. A whole reign and a vacancy stood between this ledger's own first two reigns and are now registered between them.
notes: Declared in the federation's own founding document, 19 November 1991 (promotions/uewf/archive/new-pbem-the-uewf-1991-11-19.html), which sets out how it was to be defended. Holder transcribed from the federation's own relaunch call, 14 May 1992. The federation's own World Championship semi-final of 28 December 1991 was announced in advance as crowning a champion either way — “the winner to move on to the finals of this tournament and the loser to be named the UEWF's first Atlantic Champion” — and Admiral Ax lost it. Pain's reign is renumbered r002 accordingly; how the belt passed from one to the other is not something any held document says. The weekly record survives second-hand, in another federation's own newsdesk, not yet served here. Nine editions of the WeWF's own This Week in Wrestling and its TTTTTT tag tournament, 30 January to 31 March 1992, plus the EMWA's own Kings Of The Ring of 25 March, are held in this project's own Google Groups dumps and are unserved. Between them they carry this federation's own weekly title results week by week, its full ranking tables with win-loss records and points, and two of its own matches staged play-by-play. What they say about THIS belt: The chain between the two reigns on this ledger is partly recoverable and is not one step. The table of 15 February 1992 reads "Atlantic Champion: vacant"; the same broadcast has Mosh promising to take the belt from Biff "the Terror" Jones "next week"; the roundup of 19 February has "Biff 'the Terror' Jones eeked a pin out over Mosh to become the new Atlantic Champion"; and the roundup of 25 February has "Pain succeeded in dethroning new Atlantic Champion Biff 'The Terror' Jone[s]." So: Admiral Ax (28 December 1991, r001 here) … vacancy … Biff "the Terror" Jones (c. 19 February 1992) … Pain (c. 25 February 1992, r002 here). At least one whole reign and one vacancy sit between the two rows this ledger carries.

name: UeWF Pacific Championship
epitaph: The Atlantic Championship's opposite number, defended on the same terms. Lord Plunder held it into the 1992 hiatus. Carried back from the WeWF wing, whose own newsdesk This Week in Wrestling printed this federation's weekly title results and full rankings through the winter of 1992. T'ien “the Master” Lung holds the belt in the newsdesk's own standings of 30 January, 15 February and 19 February 1992, and defends it over the Shropshire Slasher; Lord Plunder takes it back on 25 February with an international object. The first reign on this ledger DID NOT run unbroken to May 1992, and the row that said so is corrected.
notes: Declared in the federation's own founding document, 19 November 1991 (promotions/uewf/archive/new-pbem-the-uewf-1991-11-19.html), which sets out how it was to be defended. Holder transcribed from the federation's own relaunch call, 14 May 1992. The federation's own other World Championship semi-final, on the same night, carried the same double purpose — “The Winner will advance to face in the Championship round and the loser will be be awarded the Pacific Championship Title” — and Lord Plunder lost it to Lucifer on 28 December 1991. The reign the relaunch call recognised five months later begins there. The weekly record survives second-hand, in another federation's own newsdesk, not yet served here. Nine editions of the WeWF's own This Week in Wrestling and its TTTTTT tag tournament, 30 January to 31 March 1992, plus the EMWA's own Kings Of The Ring of 25 March, are held in this project's own Google Groups dumps and are unserved. Between them they carry this federation's own weekly title results week by week, its full ranking tables with win-loss records and points, and two of its own matches staged play-by-play. What they say about THIS belt: This belt changed hands twice inside the reign this ledger carries as one. The table of 15 February 1992 has T'ien "Master" Lung as Pacific Champion at 12-1-1, with Lord Plunder first among the contenders; the roundup of 19 February has T'ien beating the Shropshire Slasher to hold it; and the roundup of 25 February has "Lord Pluder beat Pacific Champion T'ien 'The Master' Lung by hitting him with an internation object," with the table that week reading "Pacific Champion: Lord Plunder (12-4-0)." The reign this ledger dates to 28 December 1991 therefore did NOT run unbroken to the May 1992 relaunch: T'ien Lung held the belt in between, and Lord Plunder's second reign begins in the last week of February 1992.

name: UeWF World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The federation's own senior tag belts, held by the Dangerous Emotions into the 1992 hiatus and still recognised at the relaunch. Carried back from the WeWF wing, whose own newsdesk This Week in Wrestling printed this federation's weekly title results and full rankings through the winter of 1992. The Dangerous Emotions' own manager settles the question of whether theirs is the first reign, on camera at the Boston Garden on 15 February 1992: “Now that my Emotions are the first UeWF tag-team champions, I want you to know that they will be the ONLY tag-team champions.” They are champions in the standings of 30 January and 15 February, retain by disqualification on 19 February and win by disqualification on 25 February.
notes: Declared in the federation's own founding document, 19 November 1991 (promotions/uewf/archive/new-pbem-the-uewf-1991-11-19.html), which sets out how it was to be defended. Holders transcribed from the federation's own relaunch call, 14 May 1992. It reached a final between the Armed Forces and the Dangerous Emotions — announced for a fifth night that no held document carries — so the tournament narrows this reign's start without dating it. The only surviving trace of the federation's own weekly cards rides on this belt, recorded here: the Summit's own fourth night bills the two teams contesting that semi-final as this federation's own number three and number one ranked tag teams "after three weeks of action," and has the challengers there to avenge "last week's loss to Carnage which almost knocked them out of first place." Three weeks of cards, a running ranking and at least one result between these two teams therefore existed by 30 December 1991. Not one of those cards survives anywhere in the held record, and none is structured here. The weekly record survives second-hand, in another federation's own newsdesk, not yet served here. Nine editions of the WeWF's own This Week in Wrestling and its TTTTTT tag tournament, 30 January to 31 March 1992, plus the EMWA's own Kings Of The Ring of 25 March, are held in this project's own Google Groups dumps and are unserved. Between them they carry this federation's own weekly title results week by week, its full ranking tables with win-loss records and points, and two of its own matches staged play-by-play. What they say about THIS belt: the Dangerous Emotions' own manager, interviewed on the broadcast of 15 February 1992, calls them "the first UeWF tag-team champions" — which would put the Summit's own unstaged fifth-night final their way — and the roundup of 19 February has them losing by disqualification to the Armed Forces and keeping the belts. The roundup of 25 February then has it the other way round, "The Armed forces barely held onto their title, losing to the Dangerous Emotions by DQ," which is either a title change nobody reported or the newsdesk transposing its own two teams. The contradiction is recorded rather than resolved; both documents are held and unserved.

name: UeWF Intercontinental Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The junior tag belts, held by Carnage into the 1992 hiatus and still recognised at the relaunch. Carried back from the WeWF wing, whose own newsdesk This Week in Wrestling printed this federation's weekly title results and full rankings through the winter of 1992. The Armed Forces hold this belt at 10-1-0 in the newsdesk's own standings of 30 January 1992, with Carnage ranked first behind them; Carnage hold it at 8-2-0 by 15 February and defend it twice on the record, over the Annihilation Alliance on 19 February and over the Ruffians on 25 February. An earlier reign this ledger did not carry is now registered.
notes: Declared in the federation's own founding document, 19 November 1991 (promotions/uewf/archive/new-pbem-the-uewf-1991-11-19.html), which sets out how it was to be defended. Holders transcribed from the federation's own relaunch call, 14 May 1992. Nothing in the Summit's own record bears on when this reign began. The weekly record survives second-hand, in another federation's own newsdesk, not yet served here. Nine editions of the WeWF's own This Week in Wrestling and its TTTTTT tag tournament, 30 January to 31 March 1992, plus the EMWA's own Kings Of The Ring of 25 March, are held in this project's own Google Groups dumps and are unserved. Between them they carry this federation's own weekly title results week by week, its full ranking tables with win-loss records and points, and two of its own matches staged play-by-play. What they say about THIS belt: Carnage hold it throughout — defending against the Annihilation Alliance on 19 February 1992 and against the Ruffians on the 25th — and the WeWF's own TTTTTT tournament of 24 March 1992 still bills them into its ring as "the UeWF InterContinental Tag Team Champions, CARNAGE!" Nothing in the held record says when the reign began.

name: UeWF Ladies World Championship
epitaph: Declared with the federation itself and defended, by its own rules, against the highest-ranked woman who had not had a shot that month. The division was not run again after the spring of 1992 — the president's own relaunch call says so outright. Its first champion was crowned in a ladies' battle royal on the second night of the Summit of E-Wrestling, 28 December 1991: eight women, elimination over the top rope only, and Laurie Liberty, who drew last, threw the Angel of Death out to win it. Carried back from the WeWF wing, whose own newsdesk This Week in Wrestling printed this federation's weekly title results and full rankings through the winter of 1992. Laurie Liberty is champion at 5-0-0 on 30 January and 6-0-0 on 15 February 1992. On 19 February the newsdesk rolls the finish as tape: Sarah Jackson heaves her over the top rope, Rhonda Rhodes gets in cheapshots on the outside, and “JAckson covers......ONE!....TWO.....THREEEE!!!! We've got a new champion”. Jackson keeps it on 25 February when Rhodes interferes again. The row that said “the reign is left open” is corrected.
notes: Declared in the federation's own founding document, 19 November 1991 (promotions/uewf/archive/new-pbem-the-uewf-1991-11-19.html), which sets out how it was to be defended. The discontinuation is stated in the federation's own relaunch call, 14 May 1992: "I will not be running a ladies division." Eight women, two starting and six entering at one-minute intervals, elimination over the top rope only; Laurie Liberty drew last and won it. The weekly record survives second-hand, in another federation's own newsdesk, not yet served here. Nine editions of the WeWF's own This Week in Wrestling and its TTTTTT tag tournament, 30 January to 31 March 1992, plus the EMWA's own Kings Of The Ring of 25 March, are held in this project's own Google Groups dumps and are unserved. Between them they carry this federation's own weekly title results week by week, its full ranking tables with win-loss records and points, and two of its own matches staged play-by-play. What they say about THIS belt: This reign ended, and the held record both dates and stages it. The roundup of 19 February 1992 cuts to a clip of the ladies title match and closes it on "JAckson covers......ONE!....TWO.....THREEEE!!!! We've got a new champion"; the roundup of 25 February has "Sarah Jackson kept her Women's belt, when Rhonda Rhodes interfered saving Ms. Jackson from a pinfall at the hands of Laurie Liberty." Sarah Jackson — one of the eight women of the battle royal this belt's first reign came out of — took it from Laurie Liberty in the third week of February 1992 and was still holding it a week later. No reign is minted from an unserved document; the row is corrected instead.

name: UeWF Ladies Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The HellKats and the Valkyries are the only two teams ever recorded holding these belts — the HellKats from around 30 January 1992 until the Valkyries beat them for the titles on 19 February 1992 — and the division closed with the federation's 1992 relaunch with no further holder on record.
notes: Declared in the federation's own founding document, 19 November 1991 (promotions/uewf/archive/new-pbem-the-uewf-1991-11-19.html), which sets out how it was to be defended. The discontinuation is stated in the federation's own relaunch call, 14 May 1992. That is the only sighting of this belt being contested anywhere in the record, and it is a sighting of a card that does not survive. The weekly record survives second-hand, in another federation's own newsdesk, not yet served here. Nine editions of the WeWF's own This Week in Wrestling and its TTTTTT tag tournament, 30 January to 31 March 1992, plus the EMWA's own Kings Of The Ring of 25 March, are held in this project's own Google Groups dumps and are unserved. Between them they carry this federation's own weekly title results week by week, its full ranking tables with win-loss records and points, and two of its own matches staged play-by-play. What they say about THIS belt: A holder does survive, in a document this collection holds and does not serve. The roundup of 19 February 1992 reads "The Valkyries defeated the Hellkats to become the new UeWF ladies tag team champions," and the EMWA's own Kings Of The Ring of 25 March 1992 has two TWIW women watching tapes of UeWF cards and calling the HellKats "one hell of a team." So the division ran, the belts were contested, and at least two teams held or challenged for them — none of which is minted here, because neither document is served and neither team has a row anywhere in the registry.
